question.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B=\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{A}_{1}+{x}_{2}{A}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9 & -4 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -8 \\ 5 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
